63: +  parent terminal's stdin and hangs indefinitely, emitting **nothing at all** — not a partial answer,
64: +  not an error. Because print mode buffers until completion, an empty log is also what a working
65: +  dispatch looks like mid-run, so the deadlock is indistinguishable from a slow model and has been

116: ## 3. DEFAULTS & QUICK INVOCATION
117: 
118: **cli-pi has NO fixed default model.** Pi's `--provider` default is `google` (`pi --help` documents `--provider <name> (default: google)`), but `google` is not in the authenticated roster (§2) — a dispatch that omits `--provider`/`--model` targets a provider with no authenticated model and fails on auth. Every real dispatch therefore names its provider and model explicitly; there is no skill-level default model to fall back to. The one exception is the repository's own `.pi/settings.json`, which makes `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` the default of a run that names no model, so the auth-failure consequence no longer applies inside this repository. The rule stands for every dispatch: name the provider and the model.
119: 
120: | Field | Value |
121: |-------|-------|
122: | Default model | **None** — selected per dispatch (passthrough) |
123: | Default provider (Pi's own) | `google` (not authenticated here — always override) |
124: | Default effort | None baked in — set `--thinking` explicitly per dispatch |
125: | Default mode | `--mode text` (print mode) |

130:   --model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash \

138: ## 4. REASONING-EFFORT / THINKING LEVER
139: 
140: cli-pi expresses reasoning effort through the first-class, standalone **`--thinking`** flag, independent of the `--model` id:
141: 
142: ```
143: --thinking off | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max
144: ```
145: 
146: `--thinking` is confirmed live from the installed help capture. Unlike `cli-cursor`/`cli-devin`, no effort tier is baked into any Pi model id.
147: 
148: ### Do NOT copy Codex effort syntax into Pi
149: A common, real confusion: cli-codex controls effort through config-level `-c model_reasoning_effort=...` (and `-c service_tier=...`). **Those forms are Codex-specific and must NOT be copied into a `pi` invocation.** Pi uses the bare `--thinking <tier>` flag and has no confirmed service-tier control surface.
150: 
151: ### GPT-6 effort ceilings via the `openai` provider
152: The GPT-6 tiers are reachable through Pi's `openai` provider, but Pi's `--thinking` scale tops out at `max`. Ceilings come from the cli-codex model-selection table — cross-reference [cli-codex/references/providers-and-models.md](../../cli-codex/references/providers-and-models.md) for the authoritative effort map.
153: 
154: | Model | Codex-documented effort ceiling | Reachable via Pi `--thinking`? |
155: |-------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------|
156: | `gpt-6-sol` | `ultra` | Partially — Pi's `--thinking` scale stops at `max`; `ultra` has no Pi-side value |
157: | `gpt-6-luna` | `max` | Yes — `max` is the top of Pi's own scale |
158: | `gpt-6.1-terra` | `ultra` | Partially. Pi's `--thinking` scale stops at `max`, so `ultra` has no Pi-side value |
159: 
160: Confirm the target model actually honors the requested tier before assuming it changes behavior — the contract pin did not exhaustively test every model/tier pairing.

164: ## 5. HOW TO INVOKE
165: 
166: ### Dispatch envelope (child / detached sessions)
167: When dispatching as a non-interactive child (spec-gate-neutralized worker), prefix the shared env and capture streams separately:
168: 
169: ```bash
170: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true pi -p "<prompt>" \
171:   --model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash \
172:   --thinking max --mode text --offline \
173:   </dev/null > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
174: ```
175: 
176: - `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` — neutralizes the spec-gate for a bound child worker so it does not stall waiting on an interactive Gate-3 answer.
177: - `PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true` switches the operator's global pi-blackhole package to passive, so it does not compact the child mid-run and send it back to reading. The deep-loop fan-out passes this variable through to its Pi children.
178: - **`--model` carries its provider, and the enforcement guard rejects any dispatch where it does not.** Write `--model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the split `--provider opencode-go --model deepseek-v4.1-flash` form is refused before the command is launched, whatever Pi itself would have done with it. The rule exists because an unqualified `--model` resolves against Pi's own default provider, which is `google` and unauthenticated here, so the mistake surfaces as a different model answering rather than as an error. Ids that already carry a vendor prefix simply grow a third segment, as the OpenRouter fan-out literal `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` does when it composes `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.
179: - **`</dev/null` before the redirects, on every non-interactive run.** Pi reads stdin at startup; without an EOF it waits forever, printing nothing. That is indistinguishable from a slow model, so the cost of omitting it is a hang nobody diagnoses rather than an error anyone sees.
180: - `--offline` — pass explicitly for any automated/CI dispatch; `pi --verbose` without `--offline` hung 2+ minutes with no reachable network path in the pinned contract. See [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §7 and [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) §15.
181: - **Exit code is never an availability/auth signal** — an identical unauthenticated `pi -p` returned exit `0` then exit `1` across runs. Classify the captured output text (`No API key found...`), never the exit code. See [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §9.
182: 
183: Select the headless contract deliberately: `--mode text` (print), `--mode json` (JSONL event stream), or `--mode rpc` (persistent JSONL protocol) — RPC is not a print-mode alias. See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) §4/§6/§7.

15: 
16: # cli-pi Providers, Models & Invocation
17: 
18: The single catalog of the providers, authenticated model ids, the `--thinking` effort lever, and dispatch shapes the cli-pi mode can reach. cli-pi is a multi-provider passthrough with no enforced model allowlist and no fixed default model — every dispatch names its provider and model explicitly. The repository's `.pi/settings.json` does make `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` the default of a run that names no model, but that governs only such a run and never a dispatch.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: One place to answer "which provider, which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-pi.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Choosing a `--provider <name>` + `--model <pattern>` (or a single `--model provider/id`) for a `pi` dispatch
31: - Mapping a desired reasoning effort onto the standalone `--thinking` flag
32: - Recalling the authenticated roster and the canonical non-interactive invocation shape
33: 
34: ### Core Principle
35: 
36: Unlike the sibling cli modes, cli-pi is a passthrough: it enforces no model allowlist at this layer and bakes no effort tier into any model id — provider, model, and effort are three independent choices per dispatch.
37: 
38: ### Scope
39: This file enumerates the provider/model/effort facts and the dispatch envelope. It does NOT own: the full `pi` flag surface, headless-mode contracts, auth/failure handling (see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)), the conductor/executor orchestration patterns (see [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)), per-model prompt-craft, or the fan-out / model-enforcement runtime (see §6).
40: 
41: ### Authority pointers
42: - Full CLI flags, headless modes, auth pre-flight, model selection → [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §13
43: - Dispatch envelope + failure-mode matrix → [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)
44: - Live model ids on a given install → re-read `~/.pi/agent/models-store.json` (or the in-session model picker); note `pi --list-models` returned no models on an unauthenticated run
45: - **A listing is not a probe.** `pi --list-models` prints a catalog bundled with the binary rather than asking each provider what it still serves, so a row outlives the route it names: a model withdrawn upstream keeps its row, its context figures and its capability columns, and reads as working. Before a roster row is written or a dispatch is trusted, send one real request. Read the reply text rather than the exit code, and pair it with a control on the same provider — a lone failure reads the same whether the model is gone, the credential lapsed or the balance ran out, and only the control tells those apart
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## 2. PROVIDERS & MODELS
50: 
51: > **CLOSED ROSTER — non-roster models are FORBIDDEN.** Dispatch ONLY the models listed in this section. Any model not in this roster MUST NOT be called through cli-pi. Enforcement lives in the deep-loop external-CLI fan-out, which hard-rejects any off-roster id (`isPiModelAllowed` over `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `executor-config.ts`, byte-mirrored in `fanout-run.cjs`); the `pi` binary itself is a passthrough with no allowlist, so for any direct (non-fan-out) invocation this is a **hard discipline rule**, not a runtime gate. To add a model, amend the roster (spec packet + `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS`) first — never dispatch an unlisted id ad hoc. **A provider's live catalog is not a roster.** Every gateway below fronts far more ids than this file lists, and the extra ids are forbidden exactly as an unknown provider would be: the roster is per provider, and a model allowed on one route is not thereby allowed on another.
52: 
53: Pi is a multi-provider passthrough at the binary layer. Pi's own CLI accepts either `--provider <name>` plus `--model <pattern>` or a single `--model provider/id`, but **only the single provider-qualified form is usable here** — the enforcement guard refuses the split form before launch, so every example below uses `--model provider/id`. `--model` also accepts an inline thinking suffix (`--model sonnet:high`). Reasoning effort stays independent of the model id (see §4).
54: 
55: The table below is the closed roster for cli-pi dispatch, sourced from the machine-local authenticated set (`~/.pi/agent/auth.json` + `models-store.json`; opencode-go added 2026-08-07). Re-read `models-store.json` to confirm an id is still authenticated on this machine, but do not dispatch anything outside this roster.
56: 
57: ### openai
58: 
59: Pi's built-in provider for the ChatGPT sign-in, carrying the GPT-6 personas and GPT-6.1 Terra. See the effort cross-map in §4. Pi 1.0 lists this sign-in under `openai`. The `openai-codex` name earlier Pi versions used is gone, and a dispatch to it now fails with "No API key found for openai-codex" (checked 2026-10-04 on Pi 1.0.2, where `openai/gpt-6-luna` answered). Pi exposes the base persona slugs only (no `-fast` / `-pro` speed tiers). All three ids come from Pi's own model catalog (`~/.pi/agent/models-store.json`), so `.pi/models.json` defines no `openai` models, and `pi --list-models gpt-6` confirms they resolve. Pi's catalog gained `gpt-6.1-terra` only after `pi update --models` on 2026-10-27. Before that refresh, a dispatch warned `Model "gpt-6.1-terra" not found for provider "openai". Using custom model id.` and still answered.
60: 
61: | Model id | Notes |
62: |----------|-------|
63: | `gpt-6-sol` | GPT-6 Sol |
64: | `gpt-6-luna` | GPT-6 Luna |
65: | `gpt-6.1-terra` | GPT-6.1 Terra. Dispatch-verified 2026-10-27: `pi -p --offline --model openai/gpt-6.1-terra --thinking low` replied `OK` |
66: 
67: ### minimax
68: 
69: MiniMax Direct API passthrough.
70: 
71: | Model id | Notes |
72: |----------|-------|
73: | `MiniMax-M3` | — |
74: 
75: ### opencode-go
76: 
77: OpenCode Go gateway passthrough (subsidized "2x usage" rate). Select with `--model opencode-go/<id>` — the enforced deep-loop fan-out route for both models below.
78: 
79: | Model id | Notes |
80: |----------|-------|
81: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | Latency-optimized reasoning model that takes images as well as text, pinned to `--thinking max` by policy — a tier this route carries. **The deep-loop fan-out reaches this route through the provider-qualified literal `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`**, which dispatches as `--model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at `--thinking max`; the dated bare literal `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` goes to DevPass. The two routes named the same model from 2026-09-11, when this id moved onto the gateway's own `deepseek-v4.1-flash` name and off `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`, until DevPass moved to the 2026-10-17 release; they now carry different releases, and they stay separate routes under the one-literal-one-provider rule, which is why DevPass holds the DeepSeek fan-out slot. Catalog-verified 2026-09-11 (1M context, 384K output, `images: yes`), and the route returned a real reply through its `opencode` client that same day |
82: | `qwen3.8-max` | Qwen 3.8 Max; a live `pi --provider opencode-go --model qwen3.8-max -p` dispatch completed a real turn 2026-08-07 |
83: | `glm-5.3-flash` | Z.AI GLM-5.3-Flash via the Go gateway; reasoning model whose ladder here is `low`/`high`/**`max`** — this route has no `xhigh` — dispatched at its top tier `--thinking max`; ladder re-verified in `opencode models opencode-go --verbose` on OpenCode 1 on 2026-09-04. Reachable as `--model opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash`. **Direct-dispatch route only since 2026-09-05:** the bare `glm-5.3-flash` literal now maps to `llmgateway` in `PI_MODEL_PROVIDERS`, and one literal maps to one provider, so the deep-loop fan-out reaches GLM-5.3-Flash through DevPass, not here |
84: 
85: ### llmgateway
86: 
87: DevPass (LLM Gateway) account, base `https://api.llmgateway.io/v1`, OpenAI-compatible, added to Pi **by config** — a `providers.llmgateway` block in `.pi/models.json` (`api: openai-completions`, env-keyed `${LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY}`) plus two `enabledModels` entries in `.pi/settings.json`. Not a Pi builtin; full setup, verification and removal live in [.pi/custom-providers.md](../../../../../.pi/custom-providers.md) §2. DevPass bills per token at normal API list rates; the plan buys credits at a 3x bonus, which discounts the bill rather than removing it. The gateway publishes its own per-model rates at `/v1/models`, and those are the rates carried in the `cost` blocks here. The gateway fronts many more ids than these two, and **only the two rows below are on the roster.** The undated `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is no longer registered for Pi, so pin it through OpenCode or Hermes if a run must reproduce the 2026-09-10 release.
88: 
89: Model-id gotcha: LLM Gateway takes the **bare** id, so every reference here is **two-segment** (`llmgateway/<id>`). Confirmed against the live API on 2026-09-10 — `"model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash"` returns `200`, `"model": "llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash"` returns `400 "Provider llmgateway does not support model deepseek-v4.1-flash"`. Do not send a provider-prefixed id. The gateway also rewrites ids upstream in its response (`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `zai/glm-5.3-flash`); those names are informational and must never be sent.
90: 
91: Credential: the block's `apiKey` MUST use pi's own config-value syntax, `${LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY}`, never opencode's `{env:...}`. pi has no `{env:...}` form, so it takes the braced string as a **literal** key and the gateway answers `401 Unauthorized` on the first real dispatch. Export it in `~/.zshenv` so dispatched shells inherit it. pi does not read opencode's auth store, even though both hold a key for this same account.
92: 
93: Effort policy: the ladders differ, so there is no single tier for this provider — pass `--thinking` explicitly. Pi's global `defaultThinkingLevel` is `xhigh`. GLM-5.3-Flash has a real `xhigh` above `high`, and DeepSeek marks `xhigh` unsupported so Pi's `clampThinkingLevel` rounds it UP to `max`. GPT-6 Luna is not on this provider: Pi reaches it only through `openai`.
94: 
95: **Mixed reachability, one row at a time.** `glm-5.3-flash` is **fan-out reachable through DevPass** as of 2026-09-05: the bare literal maps to `llmgateway` in `PI_MODEL_PROVIDERS`, so `${provider}/${model}` composes the two-segment `llmgateway/glm-5.3-flash` selector this gateway requires, and the opencode-go route for the same model became direct-dispatch only in exchange. DevPass took the fan-out slot on cost grounds: both bill per token, and DevPass is the cheaper of the two once the credit bonus is applied. The other bare literal here moved to `llmgateway` on 2026-09-07 for the same reason, after opencode-go's monthly window closed mid-program; the opencode-go DeepSeek route became direct-dispatch only in exchange, under the one-literal-one-provider constraint. That literal was `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` until 2026-09-10, when the gateway deactivated the id and began answering `410` for it. The bare literal then became `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, which the gateway served and which accepts images the same way. On 2026-10-17 the gateway published a second DeepSeek Flash release under its own id, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, which maps to `llmgateway` the same way; the fan-out default has moved to it, and the older literal is no longer registered for Pi, so a run that must pin the September build goes through OpenCode or Hermes.
96: 
97: | Model id | Notes |
98: |----------|-------|
99: | `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the 2026-10-17 release, via DevPass — reasoning **and images**, billed per token at normal API list rates, like every DevPass route; the account's 3x credit bonus discounts the bill, it does not make usage free. **This is the deep-loop fan-out default for DeepSeek Flash** (bare literal `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, mapped to `llmgateway`); the effort pin in `isFlashMaxPinnedModel` forces `max`, which this route accepts. It is also Pi's default model in `.pi/settings.json` and the pi-blackhole worker model at `high`. Same 1.05M context, 384K output and $0.15 in / $0.60 out per million tokens with cached reads at $0.003 as the 2026-09-10 release, and the same **effort ladder, three real levels plus off**: `none` disables thinking, `minimal` and `low` both reach **low**, `medium`, `high` and `xhigh` all reach **high** on the gateway (in Pi the map marks `xhigh` null, so `--thinking xhigh` rounds up to `max`), `max` reaches **max**, the default when nothing is sent is `high`, and this route rejects `ultra` and the integer 1-100 form. **It carries `"compat": {"supportsDeveloperRole": false}`**, for the `runware` upstream that refuses the `developer` role |
100: | `llmgateway/glm-5.3-flash` | GLM-5.3-Flash via DevPass; reasoning, full ladder including **both `xhigh` and `max`** — the only GLM-5.3-Flash route that has both. **This is the deep-loop fan-out route for GLM-5.3-Flash** (bare literal `glm-5.3-flash`, mapped to `llmgateway` since 2026-09-05); the effort pin in `isFlashMaxPinnedModel` forces `max`, a tier this route has. Context 1.05M, output 131K. Dispatch-verified 2026-09-04 at `--thinking max` |
101: 
102: Pi's `pi --help` also lists provider env vars beyond this roster (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `MINIMAX_API_KEY`, `KIMI_API_KEY`, `QWEN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY`, AWS). Documentation-only provider breadth is not a license to guess an unconfirmed model id — only the four authenticated providers above have a confirmed installed catalog.
103: 
104: **OpenRouter is off this roster, and deliberately still in the fan-out.** Direct dispatch has the
105: four providers above. The deep-loop fan-out additionally keeps two OpenRouter literals,
106: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, mapped in `PI_MODEL_PROVIDERS`.
107: Those are *distinct literals* from the bare `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and `glm-5.3-flash` rows
108: above: one literal maps to one provider, so the slash-prefixed pair composes an OpenRouter selector
109: while the bare pair composes the DevPass one. So a fan-out can still reach OpenRouter for exactly
110: those two ids. That is an operator decision, not residue the roster removal missed — do not
111: "reconcile" it by deleting the mapping, which would silently change which route those two models
112: take.
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 3. DEFAULTS & QUICK INVOCATION
117: 
118: **cli-pi has NO fixed default model.** Pi's `--provider` default is `google` (`pi --help` documents `--provider <name> (default: google)`), but `google` is not in the authenticated roster (§2) — a dispatch that omits `--provider`/`--model` targets a provider with no authenticated model and fails on auth. Every real dispatch therefore names its provider and model explicitly; there is no skill-level default model to fall back to. The one exception is the repository's own `.pi/settings.json`, which makes `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` the default of a run that names no model, so the auth-failure consequence no longer applies inside this repository. The rule stands for every dispatch: name the provider and the model.
119: 
120: | Field | Value |
121: |-------|-------|
122: | Default model | **None** — selected per dispatch (passthrough) |
123: | Default provider (Pi's own) | `google` (not authenticated here — always override) |
124: | Default effort | None baked in — set `--thinking` explicitly per dispatch |
125: | Default mode | `--mode text` (print mode) |
126: 
127: ```bash
128: # Name the provider-qualified model and the effort explicitly on every dispatch; only a run that names no model picks up the repository default:
129: pi -p "<prompt>" \
130:   --model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash \
131:   --thinking max --mode text --offline </dev/null
132: ```
133: 
134: Do not fabricate a default model when composing a cli-pi dispatch. The repository's `.pi/settings.json` default (`llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`) covers only a run that names no model, so it is not a skill-level default to lean on. If the task has no model-specific requirement, pick a provider/model from the authenticated roster (§2) deliberately and state the choice. Since 2026-10-22 the pi-blackhole worker model is `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` at `high`, and Pi's own default model is that same DevPass DeepSeek route.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## 4. REASONING-EFFORT / THINKING LEVER
139: 
140: cli-pi expresses reasoning effort through the first-class, standalone **`--thinking`** flag, independent of the `--model` id:
141: 
142: ```
143: --thinking off | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max
144: ```
145: 
146: `--thinking` is confirmed live from the installed help capture. Unlike `cli-cursor`/`cli-devin`, no effort tier is baked into any Pi model id.
147: 
148: ### Do NOT copy Codex effort syntax into Pi
149: A common, real confusion: cli-codex controls effort through config-level `-c model_reasoning_effort=...` (and `-c service_tier=...`). **Those forms are Codex-specific and must NOT be copied into a `pi` invocation.** Pi uses the bare `--thinking <tier>` flag and has no confirmed service-tier control surface.
150: 
151: ### GPT-6 effort ceilings via the `openai` provider
152: The GPT-6 tiers are reachable through Pi's `openai` provider, but Pi's `--thinking` scale tops out at `max`. Ceilings come from the cli-codex model-selection table — cross-reference [cli-codex/references/providers-and-models.md](../../cli-codex/references/providers-and-models.md) for the authoritative effort map.
153: 
154: | Model | Codex-documented effort ceiling | Reachable via Pi `--thinking`? |
155: |-------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------|
156: | `gpt-6-sol` | `ultra` | Partially — Pi's `--thinking` scale stops at `max`; `ultra` has no Pi-side value |
157: | `gpt-6-luna` | `max` | Yes — `max` is the top of Pi's own scale |
158: | `gpt-6.1-terra` | `ultra` | Partially. Pi's `--thinking` scale stops at `max`, so `ultra` has no Pi-side value |
159: 
160: Confirm the target model actually honors the requested tier before assuming it changes behavior — the contract pin did not exhaustively test every model/tier pairing.
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. HOW TO INVOKE
165: 
166: ### Dispatch envelope (child / detached sessions)
167: When dispatching as a non-interactive child (spec-gate-neutralized worker), prefix the shared env and capture streams separately:
168: 
169: ```bash
170: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true pi -p "<prompt>" \
171:   --model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash \
172:   --thinking max --mode text --offline \
173:   </dev/null > stdout.log 2> stderr.log
174: ```
175: 
176: - `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` — neutralizes the spec-gate for a bound child worker so it does not stall waiting on an interactive Gate-3 answer.
177: - `PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true` switches the operator's global pi-blackhole package to passive, so it does not compact the child mid-run and send it back to reading. The deep-loop fan-out passes this variable through to its Pi children.
178: - **`--model` carries its provider, and the enforcement guard rejects any dispatch where it does not.** Write `--model opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the split `--provider opencode-go --model deepseek-v4.1-flash` form is refused before the command is launched, whatever Pi itself would have done with it. The rule exists because an unqualified `--model` resolves against Pi's own default provider, which is `google` and unauthenticated here, so the mistake surfaces as a different model answering rather than as an error. Ids that already carry a vendor prefix simply grow a third segment, as the OpenRouter fan-out literal `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` does when it composes `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.
179: - **`</dev/null` before the redirects, on every non-interactive run.** Pi reads stdin at startup; without an EOF it waits forever, printing nothing. That is indistinguishable from a slow model, so the cost of omitting it is a hang nobody diagnoses rather than an error anyone sees.
180: - `--offline` — pass explicitly for any automated/CI dispatch; `pi --verbose` without `--offline` hung 2+ minutes with no reachable network path in the pinned contract. See [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §7 and [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) §15.
181: - **Exit code is never an availability/auth signal** — an identical unauthenticated `pi -p` returned exit `0` then exit `1` across runs. Classify the captured output text (`No API key found...`), never the exit code. See [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §9.
182: 
183: Select the headless contract deliberately: `--mode text` (print), `--mode json` (JSONL event stream), or `--mode rpc` (persistent JSONL protocol) — RPC is not a print-mode alias. See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md) §4/§6/§7.
184: 
185: ### Recursion bounds
186: A Pi session may dispatch this packet: Pi has no in-process delegation left, so the CLI is its only way to hand work out. What the shared runtime still refuses is a dispatch from inside a fan-out lineage, and one whose kind already appears in the dispatch stack.
187: 
188: ### Parallel / fan-out
189: Multi-lineage parallel dispatch is driven by `fanout-run.cjs`, which lives outside this hub — see §6.
190:

13: # cli-pi
14: 
15: > Dispatch a scoped task to Pi's terminal coding agent and return validated code, analysis, JSON events or RPC results to the calling runtime.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
20: 
21: | Aspect | What you get |
22: |---|---|
23: | **Use it for** | Headless Pi coding, read-only tool-constrained review, JSON event output, RPC integration and Pi resource inspection |
24: | **Invoke with** | "pi cli", "pi agent", "pi.dev cli", "delegate to pi" or "pi coding agent" |
25: | **Works on** | An external runtime that can reach the pi binary and the shared deep-loop executor |
26: | **Produces** | Validated text, JSONL event output, RPC handback or workspace changes |
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. OVERVIEW
31: 
32: ### Why This Skill Exists
33: 
34: A calling AI that wants Pi's headless surfaces has no safe shortcut. Hand-building a dispatch risks malformed flags, a failed provider call treated as success or a surface mismatch. Pi exposes more than one headless surface. Its JSON event mode and persistent RPC mode require different consumers. The local contract pin confirms the core command shape and the unreliable failure exit-code behavior. See the [pinned contract](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
35: 
36: That is the whole reason this skill exists. It makes Pi reachable as a controlled headless surface: probe the binary, pick the output contract and delegate execution to the shared deep-loop runtime. The calling AI stays the conductor and validates what comes back. The skill is not a launcher for one command. Matching the consumer to the right surface is the point.
37: 
38: ### What It Does
39: 
40: cli-pi probes for the pi binary, selects the requested headless surface and delegates process execution to the shared deep-loop runtime. It keeps Pi-native skills, prompt templates, extensions, MCP and community packages in separate references, so documentation-only behavior is not mistaken for live verification.
41: 
42: ### The Output Contract Layer
43: 
44: | Contract | What the skill returns | When it earns its place |
45: |---|---|---|
46: | **Print** | Validated text from a one-shot headless run | A single task with read-only tool constraints |
47: | **JSON** | One JSON object per line as an event stream | A consumer that parses structured output |
48: | **RPC** | A persistent stdin/stdout JSONL protocol | A long-lived integration with a JSONL client |
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. QUICK START
53: 
54: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
55: 
56: ~~~bash
57: command -v pi
58: ~~~
59: 
60: Success prints the path to the Pi executable. If it prints nothing, stop before constructing a dispatch.
61: 
62: **Step 2: Choose the output contract.**
63: 
64: ~~~bash
65: pi -p "Review the authentication flow and report findings" --mode text --tools read,grep,find,ls
66: ~~~
67: 
68: This is the read-only tool-constrained print pattern from the live help capture. Validate the output before relying on it.
69: 
70: **Step 3: Use structured output only when the consumer is ready.**
71: 
72: ~~~bash
73: pi --mode json "Summarize the changed files"
74: ~~~
75: 
76: JSON mode emits one JSON object per line. For a persistent integration, use pi --mode rpc and a JSONL client. See [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md).
77: 
78: ---
79: 
80: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
81: 
82: ### The Conductor Model
83: 
84: The calling AI remains the conductor. It classifies the task, selects the output contract, composes a scoped prompt and sends it to the shared runtime. The runtime launches Pi and returns output. The caller checks provider errors, extension errors, changed files and tests. Print mode is the one-shot path. JSON mode is an event stream. RPC is a long-lived stdin/stdout protocol.
85: 
86: The pinned contract confirms these distinctions, while native skills and prompt-template discovery remain documented but unconfirmed for this packet. The exact source links and confidence labels live in [native-skills-and-extensions.md](./references/native-skills-and-extensions.md).
87: 
88: Prompt quality follows the shared two-tier rule in [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md). The card delegates framework selection to sk-prompt and adds only Pi dispatch mechanics.
89: 
90: ### The Conservative Guard
91: 
92: The packet's guard is conservative. Process ancestry is checked first, then a .pi project-directory heuristic is checked. Neither the absence of a signal nor the presence of a directory proves that a session is active. A detected signal stops dispatch.
93: 
94: ---
95:

97:

167: ## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING
168: 
169: | What you see | Why | Fix |
170: |---|---|---|
171: | pi is not found | The binary is absent from PATH | Install the Pi package, refresh PATH, then rerun command -v pi |
172: | Missing provider API key | Pi cannot reach the selected model | Configure provider auth and retry, then inspect the output text. Do not rely on the exit code |
173: | Different failure exit codes | The pinned contract observed exit 0 and exit 1 for similar unauthenticated runs | Inspect output text and classify the failure |
174: | Extension load failure | An extension can block the session when its export is invalid | Remove or fix the extension, then rerun with the required validation |
175: | JSON consumer hangs or misparses | JSON mode is line-delimited and RPC is persistent | Choose one contract and parse JSONL records correctly |
176: | Package install asks for trust | Project-local package changes need approval | Review the package and approve project-local changes explicitly |

180: ## 8. FAQ
181:

30: ## 2. OVERVIEW
31: 
32: ### Why This Skill Exists
33: 
34: A calling AI that wants Pi's headless surfaces has no safe shortcut. Hand-building a dispatch risks malformed flags, a failed provider call treated as success or a surface mismatch. Pi exposes more than one headless surface. Its JSON event mode and persistent RPC mode require different consumers. The local contract pin confirms the core command shape and the unreliable failure exit-code behavior. See the [pinned contract](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
35: 
36: That is the whole reason this skill exists. It makes Pi reachable as a controlled headless surface: probe the binary, pick the output contract and delegate execution to the shared deep-loop runtime. The calling AI stays the conductor and validates what comes back. The skill is not a launcher for one command. Matching the consumer to the right surface is the point.
37: 
38: ### What It Does
39: 
40: cli-pi probes for the pi binary, selects the requested headless surface and delegates process execution to the shared deep-loop runtime. It keeps Pi-native skills, prompt templates, extensions, MCP and community packages in separate references, so documentation-only behavior is not mistaken for live verification.
41:

46: | **Print** | Validated text from a one-shot headless run | A single task with read-only tool constraints |
47: | **JSON** | One JSON object per line as an event stream | A consumer that parses structured output |
48: | **RPC** | A persistent stdin/stdout JSONL protocol | A long-lived integration with a JSONL client |
49:

52: ## 3. QUICK START

54: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**

57: command -v pi
58: ~~~
59:

61: 
62: **Step 2: Choose the output contract.**
63: 
64: ~~~bash
65: pi -p "Review the authentication flow and report findings" --mode text --tools read,grep,find,ls
66: ~~~
67: 
68: This is the read-only tool-constrained print pattern from the live help capture. Validate the output before relying on it.
69: 
70: **Step 3: Use structured output only when the consumer is ready.**

72: ~~~bash

74: ~~~
75: 
76: JSON mode emits one JSON object per line. For a persistent integration, use pi --mode rpc and a JSONL client. See [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md).
77: 
78: ---

80: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
81: 
82: ### The Conductor Model
83: 
84: The calling AI remains the conductor. It classifies the task, selects the output contract, composes a scoped prompt and sends it to the shared runtime. The runtime launches Pi and returns output. The caller checks provider errors, extension errors, changed files and tests. Print mode is the one-shot path. JSON mode is an event stream. RPC is a long-lived stdin/stdout protocol.
85: 
86: The pinned contract confirms these distinctions, while native skills and prompt-template discovery remain documented but unconfirmed for this packet. The exact source links and confidence labels live in [native-skills-and-extensions.md](./references/native-skills-and-extensions.md).
87: 
88: Prompt quality follows the shared two-tier rule in [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md). The card delegates framework selection to sk-prompt and adds only Pi dispatch mechanics.
89: 
90: ### The Conservative Guard
91: 
92: The packet's guard is conservative. Process ancestry is checked first, then a .pi project-directory heuristic is checked. Neither the absence of a signal nor the presence of a directory proves that a session is active. A detected signal stops dispatch.

8: # Pi CLI Orchestrator - Cross-AI Task Delegation
9: 
10: > **A Pi session MAY dispatch this skill.** Pi has no in-process delegation of its own, so the CLI
11: > is the only way a Pi session can hand work out; being inside Pi is not a reason to refuse.
12: >
13: > What still refuses: the shared runtime rejects a dispatch from inside a fan-out lineage, and one
14: > whose kind already appears in the dispatch stack. Those bound a runaway spawn chain and are
15: > unchanged. The sibling cli-X packets keep their own guards; this carve-out is Pi's alone.
16: 
17: Orchestrate Pi's terminal coding agent for headless coding, read-only tool-constrained reviews, JSON event-stream integrations, RPC clients, and Pi-native resource discovery.
18: The pinned contract is the source for confirmed command behavior: [Pi contract pin](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
19: Pi-native skills, prompt templates, and some package surfaces remain documented but unconfirmed unless a source says otherwise.
20: 
21: **Core principle**: use Pi for the surfaces it exposes, delegate research and review lineages to the shared runtime, validate the returned output, and keep the calling AI as conductor.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
26: 
27: ### Activation Triggers
28: 
29: - **Headless Pi dispatch**: use when the task explicitly requests Pi, pi.dev, or the Pi coding agent.
30: - **Cross-AI validation**: use for an independent implementation attempt, code review, or second opinion through Pi.
31: - **JSON event output**: use when a caller needs Pi's line-delimited event stream.
32: - **RPC integration**: use when a long-lived stdin/stdout protocol is explicitly requested.
33: - **Pi-native resources**: use when the task concerns Pi skills, prompt templates, extensions, or installed packages.
34: - **Community package delegation**: use when the task explicitly names pi-mcp-extension.
35: 
36: ### When NOT to Use
37: 
38: - Pi is not installed or cannot be found on PATH.
39: - The task is a small in-process change that the calling AI already understands.
40: - The task requires a feature that belongs to the shared deep-loop runtime rather than this packet.
41: - A community package is requested without approval to install or trust project-local files.
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
46: 
47: The `cli-external-orchestration` hub routes a Pi dispatch here: the request names Pi, pi.dev or the Pi coding agent, or needs Pi's JSON event stream, an RPC client, an independent second opinion, or Pi-native skills, extensions and packages.
48: `hub-router.json` scores that request, the winning `workflowMode` is `cli-pi`, and the hub loads this `SKILL.md` first.
49: The hub root `ROUTER.md` names this packet's first leaves, so leaf selection stays in the hub router rather than in this file.
50: `command -v pi` decides whether the route exists at all, and the probe runs before every dispatch.
51: It loads `references/cli-reference.md` and `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` first on every run, before any intent selection.
52: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
57: 
58: ### Execution Ownership
59: 
60: This packet owns provider-specific routing, the availability probe, and prompt construction.
61: For research and review lineages, the shared deep-loop runtime owns process construction and execution. The runtime supports the `cli-pi` executor kind, and its fan-out command builder is implemented with print mode, a provider-qualified `--model`, and `--thinking` from `reasoningEffort`, so a lineage dispatches through the executor kind directly.
62: That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
63: Do not add a packet-local wrapper, spawn path, or command builder.
64: 
65: **Four providers are reachable:** `openai` (the ChatGPT sign-in, named `openai-codex` before Pi 1.0), `opencode-go`, `llmgateway` (**DevPass**, the operator's LLM Gateway plan, metered per token with a 3x credit bonus) and `minimax`.
66: `llmgateway` is not a Pi builtin. It exists only because `.pi/models.json` declares it, and its setup, credentials and removal are in [.pi/custom-providers.md](../../../../.pi/custom-providers.md).
67: 
68: **Closed roster: non-roster models are FORBIDDEN.** Dispatch ONLY the models in [references/providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §2. That file is the single place the ids, thinking ceilings and per-provider id shapes are recorded, and this file names the providers without restating their models.
69: The deep-loop fan-out hard-rejects any off-roster id (`isPiModelAllowed` over `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS`). Even a direct `pi --model` invocation must not use an unlisted id.
70: To add a model, amend the roster first, in the spec packet and in `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS`.
71: 
72: The pinned contract confirms that headless Pi uses print mode, that JSON mode emits JSONL events, and that RPC mode is a persistent JSONL protocol. These are different contracts. Do not treat RPC as a one-shot print invocation. See [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) and [integration-patterns.md](./references/integration-patterns.md).
73: 
74: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
75: 
76: The full flag glossary and pinned-contract citations are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
77: 
78: - **Redirect stdin on every non-interactive dispatch: `</dev/null`.** Without it `pi -p` inherits the
79:   parent terminal's stdin and hangs indefinitely, emitting **nothing at all** — not a partial answer,
80:   not an error. Because print mode buffers until completion, an empty log is also what a working
81:   dispatch looks like mid-run, so the deadlock is indistinguishable from a slow model and has been
82:   mistaken for one for over an hour. The sibling `cli-opencode` packet carries the same rule for
83:   `opencode run`; it applies here for exactly the same reason.
84: - **`--offline` is required for any automated or CI dispatch.** `pi --verbose` without `--offline` hung for over two minutes with no reachable network path in the pinned contract's live probe. Any non-interactive dispatch through this packet must pass `--offline` explicitly rather than rely on a fast failure.
85: - **The exit code is never an availability or auth signal.** An identical unauthenticated `pi -p` dispatch returned exit `0` on the first run and exit `1` on every subsequent run in the pinned contract. Every guard in this packet checks output text (`No API key found...`), never exit code.
86: - **An invalid `.pi/extensions/*.ts` fails the whole session, not just that extension.** The pinned contract confirmed Pi validates extensions must export a factory function; a broken one blocks the entire dispatch with `Extension does not export a valid factory function` rather than skipping it with a warning.
87: - **The default provider is `google`, not Anthropic.** `pi --help` documents `--provider <name> (default: google)`. Do not assume an Anthropic-first default when you compose a dispatch that omits `--provider`.
88:   This repository's `.pi/settings.json` overrides that builtin: `defaultProvider` is `llmgateway` and `defaultModel` is `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, so a run naming no model goes there rather than to `google`.
89: - **`pi install`/`pi list` require `--approve` to see or modify project-local package config.** Without it, both commands behave as if no packages exist, even when one is installed — the trust gate applies to reads, not only writes.
90: - **The operator's global Pi packages load in a dispatched child, and pi-blackhole compacts it mid-run.** pi-blackhole's config (`~/.pi/agent/pi-blackhole/pi-blackhole-config.json`) auto-compacts at `compactAfterTokens`, 272,000 here, with `midRunCompaction: "resume"`.
91:   The compaction replaces everything the child has read with a structural summary, so a child still reading when it fires starts reading again and can loop without ever editing.
92:   Set `PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true` in the child's environment, which the package documents as switching off its background workers and its auto-compaction.
93:   The deep-loop fan-out's cli-pi environment filter passes this one variable through, so a value exported in the shell that runs the fan-out reaches every Pi child, and any variable outside the filter's list is still stripped.
94:   Pi's own compaction is off in `.pi/settings.json`, so the child keeps its model's full context window.
95: 
96: ### Dispatch Lifecycle
97: 
98: 1. Verify the binary with command -v pi.
99: 2. Classify the request as print, JSON, RPC, read-only tool-constrained review, native-resource inspection, or generation.
100: 3. Compose the prompt using [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md).
101: 4. Pass a research or review lineage to the shared deep-loop runtime; run a single build or doc dispatch with the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
102: 5. Capture stdout and stderr separately when the runtime allows it.
103: 6. Validate the output, changed files, and required tests before handback.
104: 
105: ### Headless Modes
106: 
107: | Requested result | Pi surface | Guardrail |
108: |---|---|---|
109: | One prompt and final response | print mode with -p or --print | Inspect output, not exit code alone |
110: | Structured events | --mode json | Parse one JSON object per line |
111: | Long-lived integration | --mode rpc | Keep stdin/stdout as a JSONL protocol |
112: | Read-only review | print mode plus --tools read,grep,find,ls | Treat the tool allowlist as the write boundary |
113: 
114: The print, JSON, RPC, and tool flags above are from the live help capture and the pinned contract. The read-only pattern is a caller-selected restriction, not a separate Pi plan mode.
115: 
116: ### Provider Preflight
117: 
118: Pi reports missing provider credentials in output. The pinned contract observed the same failure with different exit codes across otherwise identical invocations. Never use an exit code alone to claim that a dispatch reached a model. If the output reports a missing API key, stop and surface the provider requirement.
119: 
120: ### Native Resources
121: 
122: Pi's native resource surfaces are documented separately because their discovery behavior is not uniformly live-confirmed:
123: 
124: - [native-skills-and-extensions.md](./references/native-skills-and-extensions.md) covers skills, prompt templates, and extensions.
125: - [mcp-and-third-party-packages.md](./references/mcp-and-third-party-packages.md) covers packages, MCP, and community bridges.
126: - [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) covers Pi's built-in tool surface and the delegation boundary.
127: 
128: ### Classifier Calls
129: 
130: Pi carries classifier models that answer a typed question over JSON state instead of chatting. The
131: classifier types are `choice`, `bool` and `score`, documented in the installed package's
132: `docs/models.md`. A Pi worker reaches them three ways:
133: 
134: - a codemode script calls `models.getModelOfType("classifier", provider, id)`, then
135:   `models.classify(model, { state, questions })`, and needs `"defaultTools": ["+codemode"]` in settings
136: - an extension calls `ctx.modelRegistry.classify()` and needs no codemode
137: - the SDK's `ModelRuntime` exposes `create()`, `getModelOfType`, `getAvailableOfType` and `classify`
138: 
139: Credentials stay in Pi's own store. Pi resolves them from its own configuration, so a classifier call
140: passes no key, and an answer is evidence for the caller's decision, never permission. When the service
141: reports token counts, `result.usage` carries them with their cost.
142: 
143: ### Prompt Construction
144: 
145: The caller remains responsible for task scope, files, acceptance criteria, and verification. Use the prompt templates as scaffolds, not as a substitute for reading the target mode's skill contract. Pass an established spec folder to a non-interactive child when the parent workflow requires it.
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## 4. RULES
150: 
151: ### ✅ ALWAYS
152: 
153: 1. Run command -v pi before every dispatch.
154: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to the shared deep-loop runtime. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
155: 3. Choose print, JSON, or RPC deliberately. RPC is persistent and is not a print-mode alias.
156: 4. Capture and inspect output text for provider and extension failures.
157: 5. Use the prompt-quality card's two-tier precedence rule.
158: 6. Apply the least-permissive tool set that satisfies the task.
159: 7. Validate Pi-generated changes with the repository's code and test gates.
160: 8. Keep the current runtime as conductor and Pi as delegated executor.
161: 9. Treat Pi-native discovery claims as confirmed only when backed by the pinned contract or a linked live documentation page.
162: 10. Compose every dispatch as `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9; never hardcode a runtime) and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown).
163:    Core Pi has no native persona surface on `pi -p`, so INLINE the persona block into the payload, because the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
164:    A persona-less leaf runs as a generic assistant, dropping its tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
165: 11. Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt. The variable makes the waiver true. It does not make it observable.
166:    The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.

2: name: cli-pi
3: description: "Pi CLI executor for guarded headless coding, JSON/RPC integration, native skills/extensions, and community-package delegation."
4: allowed-tools: [Bash, Read, Glob, Grep]

6: ---
7: 
8: # Pi CLI Orchestrator - Cross-AI Task Delegation
9: 
10: > **A Pi session MAY dispatch this skill.** Pi has no in-process delegation of its own, so the CLI
11: > is the only way a Pi session can hand work out; being inside Pi is not a reason to refuse.
12: >
13: > What still refuses: the shared runtime rejects a dispatch from inside a fan-out lineage, and one
14: > whose kind already appears in the dispatch stack. Those bound a runaway spawn chain and are
15: > unchanged. The sibling cli-X packets keep their own guards; this carve-out is Pi's alone.
16: 
17: Orchestrate Pi's terminal coding agent for headless coding, read-only tool-constrained reviews, JSON event-stream integrations, RPC clients, and Pi-native resource discovery.
18: The pinned contract is the source for confirmed command behavior: [Pi contract pin](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
19: Pi-native skills, prompt templates, and some package surfaces remain documented but unconfirmed unless a source says otherwise.
20: 
21: **Core principle**: use Pi for the surfaces it exposes, delegate research and review lineages to the shared runtime, validate the returned output, and keep the calling AI as conductor.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
26: 
27: ### Activation Triggers
28: 
29: - **Headless Pi dispatch**: use when the task explicitly requests Pi, pi.dev, or the Pi coding agent.
30: - **Cross-AI validation**: use for an independent implementation attempt, code review, or second opinion through Pi.
31: - **JSON event output**: use when a caller needs Pi's line-delimited event stream.
32: - **RPC integration**: use when a long-lived stdin/stdout protocol is explicitly requested.
33: - **Pi-native resources**: use when the task concerns Pi skills, prompt templates, extensions, or installed packages.
34: - **Community package delegation**: use when the task explicitly names pi-mcp-extension.
35: 
36: ### When NOT to Use
37: 
38: - Pi is not installed or cannot be found on PATH.
39: - The task is a small in-process change that the calling AI already understands.
40: - The task requires a feature that belongs to the shared deep-loop runtime rather than this packet.
41: - A community package is requested without approval to install or trust project-local files.
42: 
43: ---
44: 
45: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
46: 
47: The `cli-external-orchestration` hub routes a Pi dispatch here: the request names Pi, pi.dev or the Pi coding agent, or needs Pi's JSON event stream, an RPC client, an independent second opinion, or Pi-native skills, extensions and packages.
48: `hub-router.json` scores that request, the winning `workflowMode` is `cli-pi`, and the hub loads this `SKILL.md` first.
49: The hub root `ROUTER.md` names this packet's first leaves, so leaf selection stays in the hub router rather than in this file.
50: `command -v pi` decides whether the route exists at all, and the probe runs before every dispatch.
51: It loads `references/cli-reference.md` and `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` first on every run, before any intent selection.
52: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
57: 
58: ### Execution Ownership
59: 
60: This packet owns provider-specific routing, the availability probe, and prompt construction.
61: For research and review lineages, the shared deep-loop runtime owns process construction and execution. The runtime supports the `cli-pi` executor kind, and its fan-out command builder is implemented with print mode, a provider-qualified `--model`, and `--thinking` from `reasoningEffort`, so a lineage dispatches through the executor kind directly.
62: That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
63: Do not add a packet-local wrapper, spawn path, or command builder.
64: 
65: **Four providers are reachable:** `openai` (the ChatGPT sign-in, named `openai-codex` before Pi 1.0), `opencode-go`, `llmgateway` (**DevPass**, the operator's LLM Gateway plan, metered per token with a 3x credit bonus) and `minimax`.
66: `llmgateway` is not a Pi builtin. It exists only because `.pi/models.json` declares it, and its setup, credentials and removal are in [.pi/custom-providers.md](../../../../.pi/custom-providers.md).
67: 
68: **Closed roster: non-roster models are FORBIDDEN.** Dispatch ONLY the models in [references/providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §2. That file is the single place the ids, thinking ceilings and per-provider id shapes are recorded, and this file names the providers without restating their models.
69: The deep-loop fan-out hard-rejects any off-roster id (`isPiModelAllowed` over `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS`). Even a direct `pi --model` invocation must not use an unlisted id.
70: To add a model, amend the roster first, in the spec packet and in `PI_SUPPORTED_MODELS`.
71: 
72: The pinned contract confirms that headless Pi uses print mode, that JSON mode emits JSONL events, and that RPC mode is a persistent JSONL protocol. These are different contracts. Do not treat RPC as a one-shot print invocation. See [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) and [integration-patterns.md](./references/integration-patterns.md).
73: 
74: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
75: 
76: The full flag glossary and pinned-contract citations are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
77: 
78: - **Redirect stdin on every non-interactive dispatch: `</dev/null`.** Without it `pi -p` inherits the
79:   parent terminal's stdin and hangs indefinitely, emitting **nothing at all** — not a partial answer,
80:   not an error. Because print mode buffers until completion, an empty log is also what a working
81:   dispatch looks like mid-run, so the deadlock is indistinguishable from a slow model and has been
82:   mistaken for one for over an hour. The sibling `cli-opencode` packet carries the same rule for
83:   `opencode run`; it applies here for exactly the same reason.
84: - **`--offline` is required for any automated or CI dispatch.** `pi --verbose` without `--offline` hung for over two minutes with no reachable network path in the pinned contract's live probe. Any non-interactive dispatch through this packet must pass `--offline` explicitly rather than rely on a fast failure.
85: - **The exit code is never an availability or auth signal.** An identical unauthenticated `pi -p` dispatch returned exit `0` on the first run and exit `1` on every subsequent run in the pinned contract. Every guard in this packet checks output text (`No API key found...`), never exit code.
86: - **An invalid `.pi/extensions/*.ts` fails the whole session, not just that extension.** The pinned contract confirmed Pi validates extensions must export a factory function; a broken one blocks the entire dispatch with `Extension does not export a valid factory function` rather than skipping it with a warning.
87: - **The default provider is `google`, not Anthropic.** `pi --help` documents `--provider <name> (default: google)`. Do not assume an Anthropic-first default when you compose a dispatch that omits `--provider`.
88:   This repository's `.pi/settings.json` overrides that builtin: `defaultProvider` is `llmgateway` and `defaultModel` is `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, so a run naming no model goes there rather than to `google`.
89: - **`pi install`/`pi list` require `--approve` to see or modify project-local package config.** Without it, both commands behave as if no packages exist, even when one is installed — the trust gate applies to reads, not only writes.
90: - **The operator's global Pi packages load in a dispatched child, and pi-blackhole compacts it mid-run.** pi-blackhole's config (`~/.pi/agent/pi-blackhole/pi-blackhole-config.json`) auto-compacts at `compactAfterTokens`, 272,000 here, with `midRunCompaction: "resume"`.
91:   The compaction replaces everything the child has read with a structural summary, so a child still reading when it fires starts reading again and can loop without ever editing.
92:   Set `PI_BLACKHOLE_PASSIVE=true` in the child's environment, which the package documents as switching off its background workers and its auto-compaction.
93:   The deep-loop fan-out's cli-pi environment filter passes this one variable through, so a value exported in the shell that runs the fan-out reaches every Pi child, and any variable outside the filter's list is still stripped.
94:   Pi's own compaction is off in `.pi/settings.json`, so the child keeps its model's full context window.
95: 
96: ### Dispatch Lifecycle
97: 
98: 1. Verify the binary with command -v pi.
99: 2. Classify the request as print, JSON, RPC, read-only tool-constrained review, native-resource inspection, or generation.
100: 3. Compose the prompt using [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md).
101: 4. Pass a research or review lineage to the shared deep-loop runtime; run a single build or doc dispatch with the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
102: 5. Capture stdout and stderr separately when the runtime allows it.
103: 6. Validate the output, changed files, and required tests before handback.
104: 
105: ### Headless Modes
106: 
107: | Requested result | Pi surface | Guardrail |
108: |---|---|---|
109: | One prompt and final response | print mode with -p or --print | Inspect output, not exit code alone |
110: | Structured events | --mode json | Parse one JSON object per line |
111: | Long-lived integration | --mode rpc | Keep stdin/stdout as a JSONL protocol |
112: | Read-only review | print mode plus --tools read,grep,find,ls | Treat the tool allowlist as the write boundary |
113: 
114: The print, JSON, RPC, and tool flags above are from the live help capture and the pinned contract. The read-only pattern is a caller-selected restriction, not a separate Pi plan mode.
115: 
116: ### Provider Preflight
117: 
118: Pi reports missing provider credentials in output. The pinned contract observed the same failure with different exit codes across otherwise identical invocations. 121: 
122: Pi's native resource surfaces are documented separately because their discovery behavior is not uniformly live-confirmed:
123: 
124: - [native-skills-and-extensions.md](./references/native-skills-and-extensions.md) covers skills, prompt templates, and extensions.
125: - [mcp-and-third-party-packages.md](./references/mcp-and-third-party-packages.md) covers packages, MCP, and community bridges.
126: - [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) covers Pi's built-in tool surface and the delegation boundary.
127: 
128: ### Classifier Calls
129: 
130: Pi carries classifier models that answer a typed question over JSON state instead of chatting. The
131: classifier types are `choice`, `bool` and `score`, documented in the installed package's
132: `docs/models.md`. A Pi worker reaches them three ways:
133: 
134: - a codemode script calls `models.getModelOfType("classifier", provider, id)`, then
135:   `models.classify(model, { state, questions })`, and needs `"defaultTools": ["+codemode"]` in settings
136: - an extension calls `ctx.modelRegistry.classify()` and needs no codemode
137: - the SDK's `ModelRuntime` exposes `create()`, `getModelOfType`, `getAvailableOfType` and `classify`

140: passes no key, and an answer is evidence for the caller's decision, never permission. When the service
141: reports token counts, `result.usage` carries them with their cost.
142:

144: 
145: The caller remains responsible for task scope, files, acceptance criteria, and verification. Use the prompt templates as scaffolds, not as a substitute for reading the target mode's skill contract. Pass an established spec folder to a non-interactive child when the parent workflow requires it.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Covers Pi capabilities that are exclusive, or meaningfully different in shape, compared to the other 5 CLI executors this hub dispatches, so the calling AI can route a task to Pi specifically for one of these surfaces rather than by habit.

- Choosing whether a task needs Pi's persistent RPC surface instead of a one-shot print dispatch
- Understanding why Pi's extension/prompt-template system is first-party where sibling CLIs need a package or a hooks-config file
- Scoping a dispatch to Pi's minimal built-in tool set via `--tools`
- Picking a reasoning-effort tier via `--thinking` when the task's model supports it

| Tool | Purpose |
| ------| ---------|

Free text uses the ripgrep recipes in `system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md`, over spec docs and skill docs only. A miss is a clean no-hit. Scope and declared losses: `system-spec-kit` SKILL.md §3. |

#### Git Workspace Safety

- **Ask before every push to a branch outside sk-git's remote allowlist.** A prior approval never carries forward. An explicit push instruction is itself the go-ahead.

15: # Pi MCP and Third-Party Packages
16: 
17: This reference separates Pi's first-party CLI from community packages that extend it.
18: 
19: Phase 007 confirmed pi-mcp-extension's stdio transport live. It did not live-verify a full successful provider-backed dispatch through the package. Source: [Pi contract pin](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Separates confirmed first-party Pi behavior from community-package behavior, and tracks which transports and install paths have moved from documented-only to live-confirmed.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - A request names MCP, pi-mcp-extension, stdio, streamable HTTP, SSE, or package installation
30: - Deciding whether a package claim is confirmed by the local pin or only by the package's own docs
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: Pi's core stays intentionally small; MCP is a third-party package (`pi-mcp-extension`), not a built-in Pi feature. A package's README is not a Pi CLI contract.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. FIRST-PARTY BOUNDARY
39: 
40: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: Pi keeps the core small and does not include built-in MCP or sub-agent workflows. Those capabilities can be added through extensions or packages. Source: [Using Pi](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/usage).
41: 
42: Therefore:
43: 
44: - Pi CLI is first-party.
45: - Pi's extension and package loading mechanism is first-party.
46: - A named npm extension is not automatically first-party.
47: - A package's README is not a Pi contract.
48: - This packet must label package behavior separately.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 3. PI-MCP-EXTENSION
53: 
54: pi-mcp-extension is a community package, not a first-party Pi feature. Its package page is separate from the Pi CLI contract: [Pi package page](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-mcp-extension).
55: 
56: Treat the package as optional and untrusted until:
57: 
58: 1. The exact version is pinned.
59: 2. The source is reviewed.
60: 3. The project trust decision is explicit.
61: 4. The config path is isolated.
62: 5. A harmless server is tested.
63: 6. Startup and shutdown are observed.
64: 
65: **Confirmed (phase 007):** the install verb below was run live and the package was installed into `.pi/settings.json`'s `packages` array. Phase 007 confirmed `pi-mcp-extension`'s own install only.
66: 
67: ~~~bash
68: pi install npm:pi-mcp-extension
69: ~~~
70: 
71: **Confirmed (phase 007):** `.pi/mcp.json`'s stdio-transport config shape (`{command, args, env, transport: "stdio", lifecycle}`) connects live. A `pi --offline --approve` session showed `sequential_thinking` and `system-spec-memory` both connected, with `system-spec-memory`'s full real tool surface present (`memory_context`, `session_resume`, `memory_save`, `memory_delete`, etc.). That observation is a dated transport record: `system-spec-memory` has since been retired, so reproduce the check against a server the current `.pi/mcp.json` still registers. Other configured servers in that same file failed to connect in the test environment for an unrelated, already-diagnosed reason (a missing built TypeScript toolchain in that specific worktree, confirmed present in the main tree) — not a stdio-transport limitation.
72: 
73: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: streamable HTTP and SSE transport, and the package's documented global-vs-project config-override precedence. Neither has been live-tested in this packet.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 4. MCP TRANSPORT DECISION
78: 
79: Transport terms must not be conflated:
80: 
81: | Transport | Status in this packet | Safe statement |
82: |---|---|---|
83: | stdio | **Confirmed live (phase 007)** | Two stdio servers connected in the phase-007 run; both have since been retired from `.pi/mcp.json`, so re-confirm against the servers it registers now |
84: | streamable HTTP | Documented-only for pi-mcp-extension | Do not claim live connection |
85: | SSE | Documented-only for pi-mcp-extension | Do not claim live connection |
86: | Pi RPC JSONL | Confirmed as Pi's process protocol | It is not MCP transport |
87: 
88: Pi RPC and MCP are different layers. RPC connects a caller to Pi. MCP connects an extension to a tool server. See [pi-tools.md](./pi-tools.md) §2 for RPC's own sibling-comparison framing.
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 5. CONFIGURATION SCOPE
93: 
94: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: pi-mcp-extension reads an agent-level config and a project-level config, with project settings able to override global settings. Source: [pi-mcp-extension](https://pi.dev/packages/pi-mcp-extension).
95: 
96: If testing this behavior:
97: 
98: - Use a temporary project.
99: - Use a server that returns no sensitive data.
100: - Use a unique tool prefix.
101: - Capture the effective configuration.
102: - Remove the package and config afterward.
103: 
104: Never copy a production MCP configuration into a delegated prompt.
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: ## 6. INSTALL REVIEW
109: 
110: Before any package install:
111: 
112: | Question | Required answer |
113: |---|---|
114: | Is the package required? | A named task requires it |
115: | Is it community-owned? | Yes, unless the Pi project explicitly owns it |
116: | What code executes? | Extensions and package dependencies are reviewed |
117: | What files change? | Settings, lockfiles, package directories |
118: | What trust is needed? | Project-local approval is explicit |
119: | What rolls back? | Remove package and restore settings |
120: | How is it tested? | Safe server, captured logs, cleanup |
121: 
122: The package source is not an authority over the hub's routing or advisor identity.
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## 7. MCP PROMPTS
127: 
128: Use this handoff shape when a task explicitly requests MCP:
129: 
130: ~~~text
131: Package: <community package name>
132: Version: <exact version or UNKNOWN>
133: Transport: stdio | streamable-http | SSE | UNKNOWN
134: Config scope: project | global | temporary
135: Server: <non-sensitive name>

14: 
15: # Pi Native Skills and Extensions
16: 
17: This reference covers Pi's own resource model, which is distinct from this repository's skill system.
18: 
19: Confidence rule: anything marked **Per Pi docs, unconfirmed** is documentation-only for this packet. The local contract pin is the authority for live observations: [Pi contract pin](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/z_archive/031-cli-pi-creation/001-pi-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Separates Pi-native skill/prompt-template/extension discovery from this repo's own OpenCode skill packet, and tracks which of those surfaces have moved from documented-only to live-confirmed.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Deciding whether a claim about Pi's resource discovery is backed by a live test or only by Pi's own documentation
30: - Checking whether prompt templates or extensions are safe to treat as confirmed before relying on them
31: - Planning the remaining native-skill-discovery verification work
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Pi's own resource model (skills, prompt templates, extensions) is a separate consumer contract from this repository's own skill system. Confidence rule: anything marked **Per Pi docs, unconfirmed** is documentation-only; the local contract pin and phases 012/013 are the authority for live observations.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. NATIVE SKILLS
40: 
41: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: Pi implements the Agent Skills standard and loads skills from global, project, package, settings, and explicit CLI locations. See [Pi skills documentation](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/skills).
42: 
43: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: directories containing SKILL.md can be discovered recursively in skill locations, while some root markdown files are treated as individual skills. Do not use this as proof that this hub's nested packet shape will flatten safely inside Pi.
44: 
45: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: Pi reads a skill's description at startup and loads the full SKILL.md on demand. The documented model is progressive disclosure, but this packet has not live-verified the resulting prompt content in a successful provider session.
46: 
47: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: explicit --skill paths are additive and can be used with discovery controls. Check the installed help before relying on a flag in a future version.
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. REPOSITORY SKILL VERSUS PI SKILL
52: 
53: The repository's cli-pi SKILL.md is an OpenCode skill packet. Pi's native SKILL.md surface is a separate consumer contract.
54: 
55: | Concern | This repository | Pi-native surface |
56: |---|---|---|
57: | Advisor identity | Hub graph metadata | Not part of Pi's documented skill standard |
58: | Routing | mode-registry.json and hub-router.json | Per Pi docs, unconfirmed resource discovery |
59: | Runtime guard | hard-rules.json | Per Pi docs, unconfirmed loading behavior |
60: | References | Packet-local references directory | Per Pi docs, unconfirmed skill-relative resources |
61: | Verification | parent-skill-check and package validator | Per Pi docs, unconfirmed Pi validation warnings |
62: 
63: Do not copy this packet into Pi and assume the hub's single advisor identity survives. That bridge belongs to a separate integration.
64: 
65: ---
66: 
67: ## 4. PROMPT TEMPLATES
68: 
69: **Confirmed (phases 012/013):** Pi discovers flat, non-recursive markdown files under `.pi/prompts/` and exposes each as a slash command named after the file. This repo mirrors all 36 canonical `.skilled/commands/**/*.md` files this way; `sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check` reports `36 prompts are in sync`. Argument substitution — including `$ARGUMENTS` as a documented alias for `$@` — was live-confirmed in a real generated prompt file during a live session (phase 013, scenario PI-008). See [RPC documentation](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/rpc) for how prompt-template commands surface in `get_commands` output.
70: 
71: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: full path-precedence rules across every documented discovery location (global, project, package, settings, explicit CLI path) beyond the project-local `.pi/prompts/` location this packet actually populates.
72: 
73: Use [prompt-templates.md](../assets/prompt-templates.md) for caller-side dispatch templates, and see [pi-tools.md](./pi-tools.md) §4 for the sibling-comparison framing of this surface.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 5. EXTENSIONS
78: 
79: **Confirmed (phase 012):** Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*.ts` files with no settings-file registration required. This repo has 6 real extension files (`spec-gate-enforce`, `spec-gate-classify`, `dispatch-preflight-lint`, `dispatch-audit`, `post-edit-quality`, `mcp-route-guard`), each a plain `ExtensionFactory` calling `pi.on(event, handler)` against this repo's own shared guard-core modules. A live `pi --offline --approve` session loaded all 6 without a startup error. Every guard wraps its call in try/catch and fails open — a guard-core exception must never block work it merely observes.
80: 
81: The local pin also confirmed that Pi discovered a project-local `.pi/extensions/probe.ts` and failed the whole session when it exported an invalid value; replacing the stub with a callable default factory removed that specific validation error. This means an invalid extension is fail-closed at startup — distinct from, and orthogonal to, the fail-open discipline of the 6 real extensions' own internal guard logic above.
82: 
83: **Live-firing-confirmed (2026-07-28):** the extension API exposes 33 named lifecycle events (including block-capable `tool_call`), confirmed via a direct read of the installed package's `types.d.ts`, and a probe-instrumented authenticated session captured `session_start`, `input`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, and `session_shutdown(quit)` actually firing mid-dispatch with side-effect evidence (playbook scenario PI-020). Only `session_compact` remains untraced; it fires solely on manual `/compact`, the context threshold, or overflow recovery in an interactive session.
84: 
85: Per Pi docs, unconfirmed: loading from user, CLI-flag, or package locations (only the project-local `.pi/extensions/` location has been built and tested), and inspecting structured system-prompt data. See [Pi extensions documentation](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions).
86: 
87: Extension safety rules:
88: 
89: 1. Review source before enabling it.
90: 2. Keep the extension path explicit.

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |

40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro

42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:

50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"

60:

66: ```

See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

76: # Git Commit Workflows

83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?

204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
